questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
My exchange experience was significantly affected by serious administrative and structural issues related to the ECTS requirements. In practice, the host university normally only allowed exchange students to enrol in up to 20 ECTS, which directly conflicted with the home university’s and Erasmus programme’s requirement of 30 ECTS for a full-time semester.

This issue was not identified in advance but only became apparent when I personally raised the concern with my home university. This created major uncertainty about whether I would even be able to go on exchange at all and caused considerable stress during the planning process. Despite later attempts to allow some flexibility, it proved extremely difficult in practice to combine courses amounting to 30 ECTS without timetable overlaps or the risk of courses being removed.

As a result, beside countless hours of emailing, stress and a big workload  I am now missing 7 ECTS, despite having studied more than full-time during my exchange. I see this as a problem in establishing an exchange agreement that does not realistically allow students to meet the formal academic requirements in practice.

Overall, the responsibility for identifying was on me, and there this lead to a lot of diffculties since noone could tell med how they would affect my stay , which to me is highly problematic. I strongly recommend that exchange agreements are reviewed more thoroughly in advance to ensure they are actually possible and do not place students in such vulnerable academic and financial positions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I took a relatively heavy course load of 23 ECTS, which was more than the average exchange student, and the workload was high, particularly considering that even lower-credit courses (fx. 4 ECTS) required a significant amount of work. Some courses were very well taught, while others were poorly taught and quite demotivating. The experience therefore varied greatly between courses.

questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The material was generally quite understandable and not particularly difficult. However, the workload measured in hours was very high and often disproportionate to the number of credits assigned. Many courses required  mandatory attendance, and frequent assessments, which made the overall workload demanding despite the accessible level of the content.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was quite different from UCPH. It was generally more controlled and relied heavily on rote learning and memorisation.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: To be honest I think there need to be made some changes in order for this exchange relationship to function. Future students should be aware that the ECTS structure at the host institution may not align well with typical exchange requirements. But in general careful planning is essential, as the total number of credits that can realistically be taken may be limited, and timetables may not allow all desired courses to fit together. This is a structural issue with the credit system rather than the quality of teaching. But i would advise that you take your questions and doubt seriously, and demand help with the pragmatic issues.
